deities: Ketu - each deity as a Graha Lingam covered with a colored garment
festivals: Graha-shanti pujas year-round (devotees seek mitigation of malefic planetary influences)

history.period: Rebuilt 1752 by Ahom King Rajeswara Singha after the 1697 earthquake damaged the earlier temple
history.summary: The Navagraha Temple ('Temple of the Nine Planets') stands atop Chitrachal Hill (Navagraha Pahaar) in Guwahati. Its sanctum houses nine Shivalingams - the Graha Lingams - representing the nine celestial bodies of Hindu astronomy, each covered with a coloured garment symbolic of that planet, with the central lingam symbolising the Sun (Surya). An inscription records that the earlier temple was badly damaged in the great earthquake of 1697 and that Ahom King Rajeswara Singha (1751-1769) rebuilt the entire structure in 1752; an earlier 16th-century Koch foundation is speculated but unconfirmed. It is one of Assam's most ancient temples and a unique blend of faith and Vedic astronomy, where devotees perform graha-shanti pujas with bel leaves and mustard oil to pacify planetary influences. Connected to it is Silpukhuri (Silpukuri), a nine-cornered (na-kunia) tank dug in the valley south of the hill. Damaged by later earthquakes and renovated in 1923-45. The hilltop offers panoramic views over Guwahati.

name: Navagraha Temple
town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Northeast India, spread along the south bank of the Brahmaputra river in Kamrup Metropolitan district; Dispur, the capital of Assam, is its eastern suburb. Known as the 'City of Temples', it hosts Kamakhya, Umananda, Navagraha, Sukreswar and other historic shrines, plus the IIT Guwahati campus across the river. It is the gateway to the Northeast, well connected by air, rail and road.
tradition: Hinduism (graha/planetary worship within Shaivism - the nine grahas as Shivalingams)

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 20-25 km.
travel.railway: Guwahati Railway Station - nearest major railhead; taxis/autos to Chandmari.
travel.road: Hilltop temple reached by a 5-10 minute drive from the Chandmari area; good road and parking; autos and private vehicles available from any part of Guwahati city.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather, clear views from the hilltop).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Opening hours not consistently documented across sources (verify locally before visiting).
